title: Linear recurrences and rational Lambert series
summary: For a sequence $γ=(γ_n)_{n\ge 1}$, define \[ L_γ(z):=\sum_{n\ge 1}γ_n\frac{z^n}{1-z^n} =\sum_{n\ge 1}\Bigl(\sum_{d\mid n}γ_d\Bigr)z^n. \] We prove a short rigidity theorem: if $γ$ is eventually linearly recurrent and $L_γ(z)$ is rational, then $γ$ is finitely supported. Equivalently, among sequences with rational ordinary generating function, the only ones whose Lambert series is rational are the finitely supported sequences. The proof specializes the data at a finite place of a finitely generated ring and then uses the periodicity of recurrences over finite fields.
